decoys.why: Owner-only and reverts with ProtectedToken when the token is the underlying asset or the receipt token itself, so it can only move unrelated tokens; depositors' assets and receipts are untouched.

The two exit-fee helpers divide by BPS and by BPS + exitFeeBps because one prices the fee on the net amount and the other on the gross amount; both round up, withdraw rounds the receipts burned up and redeem rounds the assets down, so every rounding step goes against the caller and neither route pays a smaller fee than the other.

acceptable.note: low/design, unscored: yield arrives as a step in reportYield, so a deposit placed just before a report shares in it; the exit fee is the only brake.
low, unscored: depositCap is compared with the live balance, so yield and direct transfers consume the cap.
low, unscored: receipts sent to the contract itself cannot be recovered (sweepToken rejects the receipt token).
info, unscored: fee policy changes take effect immediately (bounded at 20% report fee and 1% exit fee).
info, unscored: decimals is the deployer-supplied asset decimals while receipts are minted at 1e6 per asset unit, so displayed balances are scaled by 1e6.

low at most, unscored: deposit has no zero-receipt guard, but with the 1e6 offset a deposit only rounds to zero after a direct transfer of about 1e6 times its size that the sender cannot recover (test_patched_P1, testFuzz_patched_P1_neverProfitable).
